questions.question: Which type of lens is thicker in the middle and thinner at the edges?

options.explanation: A concave lens is thinner in the middle and thicker at the edges.
A plano-concave lens is thinner in the middle and thicker at the edges.
A convex lens is thicker in the middle and thinner at the edges.
A plano-convex lens is not necessarily thicker in the middle and thinner at the edges.

questions.explanation: A convex lens is characterized by its shape, being thicker at the center and thinner at the edges, which causes parallel rays of light to converge.
questions.subject: upbo7-physics

questions.question: What kind of image is always formed by a concave lens, regardless of the object's position?

options.explanation: A concave lens does not form a real and inverted image.
A concave lens always forms a virtual, erect, and diminished image.
A concave lens does not form a real and enlarged image.
A concave lens does not form a virtual and inverted image.

questions.explanation: A concave lens is a diverging lens and always forms a virtual, erect, and diminished image for any position of a real object.
questions.subject: upbo7-physics

questions.question: Which type of lens is commonly used as a magnifying glass?

options.explanation: A concave lens is not typically used as a magnifying glass.
A convex lens is commonly used as a magnifying glass.
A cylindrical lens is not typically used as a magnifying glass.
A plano-concave lens is not typically used as a magnifying glass.

questions.explanation: A convex lens can form an enlarged, virtual, and erect image when the object is placed between its optical centre and focal point, which is the principle behind a magnifying glass.
questions.subject: upbo7-physics

questions.question: When an object is placed at infinity from a convex lens, where is the image formed?

options.explanation: The image is not formed at 2F when the object is at infinity.
The image is not formed between F and 2F when the object is at infinity.
The image is not formed at the optical centre when the object is at infinity.
The image is formed at the focal point (F) when the object is at infinity.

questions.explanation: Parallel rays of light coming from an object at infinity converge at the principal focus (F) after passing through a convex lens, forming a real, inverted, and highly diminished image.
questions.subject: upbo7-physics

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly differentiates a convex lens from a concave lens?

options.text: A convex lens diverges light, while a concave lens converges light.
options.explanation: This statement is incorrect, as a convex lens converges light and a concave lens diverges light.

options.text: A convex lens converges light, while a concave lens diverges light.
options.explanation: This statement is correct, as a convex lens converges light and a concave lens diverges light.

options.text: Both convex and concave lenses always converge light.
options.explanation: This statement is incorrect, as a concave lens diverges light.

options.text: Both convex and concave lenses always diverge light.
options.explanation: This statement is incorrect, as a convex lens converges light.

questions.explanation: Convex lenses are converging lenses, meaning they bend parallel light rays inwards to a focal point. Concave lenses are diverging lenses, meaning they spread parallel light rays outwards.
questions.subject: upbo7-physics

questions.question: A person suffering from hypermetropia (farsightedness) needs spectacles fitted with which type of lens?

options.explanation: A concave lens is used to correct myopia, not hypermetropia.
A convex lens is used to correct hypermetropia.
A cylindrical lens is used to correct astigmatism, not hypermetropia.
A biconcave lens is another term for a concave lens, which is used to correct myopia, not hypermetropia.

questions.explanation: Hypermetropia is a condition where the eye cannot focus on nearby objects. This is corrected by using a convex lens, which converges the light rays before they enter the eye, allowing them to focus correctly on the retina.
questions.subject: upbo7-physics

questions.question: What happens to parallel rays of light when they pass through a concave lens?

options.text: They converge at the principal focus.
options.explanation: Parallel rays of light do not converge at the principal focus when passing through a concave lens.

options.text: They appear to diverge from the principal focus.
options.explanation: Parallel rays of light appear to diverge from the principal focus when passing through a concave lens.

options.text: They continue in a straight line without bending.
options.explanation: Parallel rays of light do bend when passing through a concave lens.

options.text: They reflect back along the same path.
options.explanation: Parallel rays of light do not reflect back along the same path when passing through a concave lens.

questions.explanation: A concave lens is a diverging lens. When parallel rays of light pass through it, they spread out, appearing to originate from a virtual focal point on the same side as the object.
questions.subject: upbo7-physics

questions.question: An object is placed between the principal focus (F) and twice the focal length (2F) of a convex lens. Where will the image be formed?

options.explanation: The image is not formed at F when the object is between F and 2F.
The image is not formed at 2F when the object is between F and 2F.
The image is not formed between F and 2F when the object is between F and 2F.
The image is formed beyond 2F when the object is between F and 2F.

questions.explanation: For a convex lens, when an object is placed between F and 2F, the image formed is real, inverted, and enlarged, and is located beyond 2F on the other side of the lens.
questions.subject: upbo7-physics

questions.question: A student finds it difficult to read the blackboard from the back row of the classroom but can read a book held close to their eyes. Which type of lens should be recommended for their spectacles?

options.explanation: A concave lens is used to correct myopia.
A convex lens is used to correct hypermetropia, not myopia.
A plano-convex lens is not typically used to correct myopia.
A cylindrical lens is used to correct astigmatism, not myopia.

questions.explanation: The student is suffering from myopia (nearsightedness), where distant objects appear blurred. This condition is corrected using a concave lens, which diverges the incoming parallel rays slightly before they enter the eye, allowing them to focus correctly on the retina.
questions.subject: upbo7-physics

questions.question: How can you distinguish between a convex lens and a concave lens just by touching them, without looking?

options.text: A convex lens feels uniformly thick, while a concave lens feels thinner at the centre.

options.text: A convex lens feels thicker at the centre, while a concave lens feels thinner at the centre.
options.explanation: This statement is correct, as a convex lens is thicker in the middle and thinner at the edges, and a concave lens is thinner in the middle and thicker at the edges.

options.text: A convex lens feels thinner at the centre, while a concave lens feels uniformly thick.
options.explanation: This statement is incorrect, as a convex lens is thicker in the middle and thinner at the edges, and a concave lens is thinner in the middle and thicker at the edges.
This statement is incorrect, as a convex lens is thicker in the middle and thinner at the edges, and a concave lens is thinner in the middle and thicker at the edges.

questions.explanation: A convex lens is physically thicker in the middle and thinner at the edges. Conversely, a concave lens is thinner in the middle and thicker at the edges. This difference in physical shape can be felt by touch.

questions.question: Which type of lens is thicker in the middle and thinner at the edges?

options.explanation: A concave lens is thinner in the middle and thicker at the edges.
A convex lens is thicker in the middle and thinner at the edges.
A cylindrical lens has a different shape and is not characterized by being thicker in the middle.
A plano lens has one flat side and is not characterized by being thicker in the middle.

questions.explanation: A convex lens has a shape that bulges outwards in the middle, making it thicker at the centre and thinner at the edges.

questions.question: A lens that diverges parallel rays of light after refraction is known as a:

options.explanation: A concave lens is a diverging lens.
A convex lens is a converging lens.
A plano-convex lens is a type of converging lens.
A magnifying lens is typically a convex lens.

questions.explanation: A concave lens is also known as a diverging lens because it spreads out parallel rays of light after they pass through it.
questions.subject: upbo7-physics

questions.question: What is the nature of the image formed by a concave lens for any position of the object?

options.explanation: This is the nature of the image formed by a convex lens.
This is not the correct description of the image formed by a concave lens.
A concave lens always forms a virtual, erect, and diminished image.
This is not the correct description of the image formed by a concave lens.

questions.explanation: A concave lens always forms a virtual, erect, and diminished image, regardless of where the object is placed relative to the lens.
questions.subject: upbo7-physics

questions.question: Which type of lens is commonly used as a magnifying glass?

options.explanation: A convex lens is commonly used as a magnifying glass.
A concave lens is not typically used as a magnifying glass.
A cylindrical lens has a different shape and is not typically used as a magnifying glass.
A prism is not typically used as a magnifying glass.

questions.explanation: A convex lens, when an object is placed within its focal length, produces a magnified, virtual, and erect image, which is the principle behind a magnifying glass.
questions.subject: upbo7-physics

questions.question: The distance between the optical centre and the principal focus of a lens is called its:

options.explanation: The radius of curvature is related to the focal length but is not the same thing.
The aperture is the diameter of the lens and is not related to the focal length.
The focal length is the distance between the optical centre and the principal focus.
The principal axis is an imaginary line that passes through the optical centre and the principal focus, but it is not the same as the focal length.

questions.explanation: Focal length is the defined distance from the optical centre of a lens to its principal focus, where parallel rays converge or appear to diverge from.
questions.subject: upbo7-physics

questions.question: A person suffering from hypermetropia (farsightedness) needs spectacles fitted with which type of lens to correct their vision?

options.explanation: A concave lens is used to correct myopia (nearsightedness).
A convex lens is used to correct hypermetropia (farsightedness).
A cylindrical lens is used to correct astigmatism.
A bifocal lens is used to correct presbyopia.

questions.explanation: Hypermetropia is a vision defect where the eye cannot focus on nearby objects. A convex lens helps to converge the light rays before they enter the eye, allowing them to focus correctly on the retina.
questions.subject: upbo7-physics

questions.question: To obtain a real, inverted, and magnified image of an object using a lens, where should the object be placed relative to a convex lens?

options.explanation: At the principal focus, the image is real and inverted but not magnified.
At 2F, the image is real and inverted but not magnified.
Between F and 2F, the image is real, inverted, and magnified.
At infinity, the image is real and inverted but not magnified.

questions.explanation: When an object is placed between the principal focus (F) and twice the focal length (2F) of a convex lens, it forms a real, inverted, and magnified image.
questions.subject: upbo7-physics

questions.question: A security peephole in a door provides a wide field of view of the outside. Which type of lens is typically used in such a peephole?

options.explanation: A convex lens is not typically used in peepholes.
A concave lens is used in peepholes to provide a wide field of view.
A plano-convex lens is not typically used in peepholes.
A prism is not typically used in peepholes.

questions.explanation: A concave lens is used in peepholes because it forms a diminished (smaller) and erect image of objects over a wide angle, allowing a broader view of the area outside the door.
questions.subject: upbo7-physics

questions.question: Which statement correctly differentiates a convex lens from a concave lens based on their primary function?

options.text: A convex lens is used for myopia, while a concave lens is used for hypermetropia.
options.explanation: This statement is partially true but does not address the primary function of the lenses.

options.text: A convex lens always forms a virtual image, while a concave lens always forms a real image.
options.explanation: This statement is not accurate.

options.explanation: This statement correctly differentiates the primary function of convex and concave lenses.

questions.explanation: The fundamental difference in their optical action is that a convex lens converges (brings together) parallel light rays, whereas a concave lens diverges (spreads out) parallel light rays.

questions.question: What is the process by which living organisms take in oxygen from the air and release carbon dioxide?

options.explanation: Digestion is the process of breaking down food into nutrients, not taking in oxygen or releasing carbon dioxide.
Circulation is the process of transporting blood throughout the body, not taking in oxygen or releasing carbon dioxide.
Respiration is the biological process of taking in oxygen and releasing carbon dioxide, along with energy production, that occurs in living organisms.
Excretion is the process of removing waste products from the body, not taking in oxygen or releasing carbon dioxide.

questions.explanation: Respiration is the biological process of taking in oxygen and releasing carbon dioxide, along with energy production, that occurs in living organisms.
questions.subject: upbo7-biology

questions.question: Which gas is primarily released by humans during the process of breathing?

options.explanation: Oxygen is taken in during breathing, not released.
Carbon dioxide is produced as a waste product during respiration and is exhaled.
Nitrogen is a component of the air we breathe, but it is not primarily released by humans during breathing.
Hydrogen is not a primary gas released by humans during breathing.

questions.explanation: During respiration, oxygen is utilized, and carbon dioxide is produced as a waste product, which is then exhaled.
questions.subject: upbo7-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is the main organ for gas exchange in the human respiratory system?

options.explanation: The heart is the organ that pumps blood throughout the body, but it is not the main organ for gas exchange.
The stomach is the organ that digests food, but it is not involved in gas exchange.
The lungs are the primary organs of the human respiratory system where the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide takes place between the air and the blood.
The kidneys are the organs that filter waste and excess fluids from the blood, but they are not involved in gas exchange.

questions.explanation: The lungs are the primary organs of the human respiratory system where the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide takes place between the air and the blood.
questions.subject: upbo7-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is a product of anaerobic respiration in muscle cells during strenuous exercise?

options.explanation: Alcohol and carbon dioxide are products of anaerobic respiration in yeast, not in muscle cells during exercise.
Lactic acid is a product of anaerobic respiration in muscle cells during strenuous exercise.
Carbon dioxide and water are products of aerobic respiration, not anaerobic respiration in muscle cells during exercise.
Oxygen is not a product of anaerobic respiration in muscle cells during exercise.

questions.explanation: When there is insufficient oxygen during strenuous exercise, muscle cells switch to anaerobic respiration, producing lactic acid as a byproduct, which can cause muscle cramps.
questions.subject: upbo7-biology

questions.question: Arrange the following parts in the correct order of air passage during inhalation in humans:

options.explanation: This order is incorrect because the trachea (i) comes before the lungs (ii), and the nasal cavity (iii) comes before the trachea.
This order is incorrect because the bronchi (iv) come after the trachea (i), and the lungs (ii) come after the bronchi.
This order is correct: air enters through the nasal cavity (iii), then passes through the trachea (i), which divides into bronchi (iv), leading to the lungs (ii).
This order is incorrect because the trachea (i) comes before the bronchi (iv).

questions.explanation: Air enters through the nasal cavity, then passes through the trachea (windpipe), which divides into bronchi, leading to the lungs.
questions.subject: upbo7-biology

questions.question: Why do athletes often breathe faster and deeper after a race?

options.explanation: While breathing faster and deeper may help to reduce body temperature, it is not the primary reason athletes do so after a race.

options.text: To increase the amount of nitrogen in their blood.
options.explanation: Nitrogen is not a critical factor in this context, and increasing its amount in the blood is not a primary goal of breathing faster and deeper after exercise.

options.text: To supply more oxygen to their muscles and remove excess carbon dioxide.
options.explanation: This is the primary reason athletes breathe faster and deeper after a race: to meet the increased oxygen demand and expel excess carbon dioxide.

options.text: To produce more energy through anaerobic respiration.
options.explanation: Anaerobic respiration is not the primary goal of breathing faster and deeper after exercise; rather, it is to facilitate aerobic respiration and remove waste products.

questions.explanation: Strenuous exercise increases the demand for oxygen by muscle cells for aerobic respiration and also increases the production of carbon dioxide. Faster and deeper breathing helps to meet this increased oxygen demand and efficiently expel the excess carbon dioxide.
questions.subject: upbo7-biology

questions.question: What happens to the diaphragm during the process of inhalation?

options.text: It relaxes and moves upwards, decreasing chest cavity volume.
options.explanation: This is what happens during exhalation, not inhalation.

options.text: It relaxes and moves downwards, increasing chest cavity volume.
options.explanation: The diaphragm contracts, not relaxes, during inhalation.

options.text: It contracts and moves downwards, increasing chest cavity volume.
options.explanation: This is the correct action of the diaphragm during inhalation, which increases the chest cavity volume and draws air into the lungs.

options.text: It contracts and moves upwards, decreasing chest cavity volume.
options.explanation: This would decrease the chest cavity volume, which is the opposite of what happens during inhalation.

questions.explanation: During inhalation, the diaphragm contracts and flattens, moving downwards. This action, along with the outward movement of the ribs, increases the volume of the chest cavity, drawing air into the lungs.
questions.subject: upbo7-biology

questions.question: Which type of respiration occurs in the presence of oxygen, completely breaking down glucose to produce a large amount of energy?

options.explanation: Aerobic respiration is the process that uses oxygen to break down glucose and produce a significant amount of energy.
Anaerobic respiration does not use oxygen and does not completely break down glucose.
Fermentation is a type of anaerobic respiration that occurs in the absence of oxygen.
Photosynthesis is the process by which plants produce glucose from carbon dioxide and water, using sunlight as energy.

questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration is the process that uses oxygen to break down glucose and produce a significant amount of energy, along with carbon dioxide and water.
questions.subject: upbo7-biology

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the breathing mechanism: Which of the above statements are correct?

options.explanation: Statement (ii) is incorrect.
Both statements (ii) and (iii) are incorrect.
Both statements (i) and (iv) are correct.
Statement (ii) is incorrect.

questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct for inhalation. Statement (ii) is incorrect; the diaphragm relaxes and moves upwards during exhalation. Statement (iii) is incorrect; the volume of the chest cavity increases during inhalation. Statement (iv) is correct for exhalation as the decreased chest cavity volume increases pressure, forcing air out.
questions.subject: upbo7-biology

questions.question: Why is cellular respiration considered fundamental for the survival of almost all living organisms?

options.text: It helps in the synthesis of complex food molecules from simpler ones.
options.explanation: This describes photosynthesis, not cellular respiration.

options.text: It directly provides structural components for cell growth.
options.explanation: While cellular respiration provides energy for cell growth, it does not directly provide structural components.

options.text: It releases the chemical energy stored in food, which is essential for all life activities.
options.explanation: This is the correct reason why cellular respiration is fundamental for the survival of almost all living organisms.

options.text: It only produces oxygen, which is vital for plants.
options.explanation: Cellular respiration produces carbon dioxide and water as byproducts, and oxygen is not its primary product or purpose.

questions.explanation: Cellular respiration is the process by which cells break down glucose and other food molecules to release usable chemical energy (ATP). This energy powers all metabolic processes, growth, movement, and maintenance of life.
questions.subject: upbo7-biology

questions.question: The process by which living organisms break down food to release energy is known as:

options.explanation: Digestion is the process of breaking down food into smaller molecules, but it is not the process that directly releases energy.
Excretion is the process of removing waste products from the body, not releasing energy.
Respiration is the process by which living organisms break down food to release energy.
Circulation is the process of transporting blood throughout the body, not releasing energy.

questions.explanation: Respiration is the fundamental biological process where organisms convert nutrients into energy (ATP) for various cellular activities.
questions.subject: upbo7-biology

questions.question: Which gas is essential for aerobic respiration in most living organisms?

options.explanation: Carbon dioxide is a byproduct of aerobic respiration, not a required gas.
Nitrogen is not directly involved in aerobic respiration.
Oxygen is essential for aerobic respiration to occur.
Hydrogen is not directly involved in aerobic respiration.

questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration, which is the most common type, requires oxygen to efficiently break down glucose and release a large amount of energy.
questions.subject: upbo7-biology

questions.question: In humans, the actual exchange of gases (oxygen and carbon dioxide) takes place in which part of the lungs?

options.explanation: The trachea is the main airway that leads to the lungs, but gas exchange does not occur here.
The bronchi are airways that branch off from the trachea, but gas exchange does not occur here.
The alveoli are the site of gas exchange in the lungs.
The larynx is the voice box, and it is not involved in gas exchange.

questions.explanation: Alveoli are tiny air sacs within the lungs that have very thin walls, allowing for the efficient diffusion of oxygen into the blood and carbon dioxide out of the blood.
questions.subject: upbo7-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is an INCORRECT statement regarding anaerobic respiration?

options.text: It occurs in the absence of oxygen.
options.explanation: This statement is correct, as anaerobic respiration does occur in the absence of oxygen.

options.text: It produces less energy compared to aerobic respiration.
options.explanation: This statement is correct, as anaerobic respiration does produce less energy than aerobic respiration.

options.text: Yeast performs this type of respiration.
options.explanation: This statement is correct, as yeast does perform anaerobic respiration.

options.text: Its main products in human muscles are carbon dioxide and water.
options.explanation: This statement is incorrect, as the main product of anaerobic respiration in human muscles is lactic acid.

questions.explanation: In human muscles, the main product of anaerobic respiration is lactic acid, not carbon dioxide and water. Carbon dioxide and water are products of aerobic respiration.
questions.subject: upbo7-biology

questions.question: During strenuous exercise, muscle cramps can occur due to the accumulation of:

options.explanation: Carbon dioxide is a byproduct of aerobic respiration, not directly related to muscle cramps.
Lactic acid accumulation is the primary cause of muscle cramps during strenuous exercise.
Alcohol is not directly related to muscle cramps during exercise.
Water is not directly related to muscle cramps during exercise.

questions.explanation: When muscles work hard and oxygen supply is insufficient, they switch to anaerobic respiration, which produces lactic acid. The build-up of lactic acid causes pain and cramps.
questions.subject: upbo7-biology

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of organs through which inhaled air passes in the human respiratory system?

options.text: Nose → Trachea → Pharynx → Larynx → Bronchi → Lungs
options.explanation: This sequence is incorrect, as the pharynx comes before the larynx.

options.text: Nose → Pharynx → Larynx → Trachea → Bronchi → Lungs
options.explanation: This is the correct sequence of organs in the human respiratory system.

options.text: Nose → Larynx → Pharynx → Trachea → Bronchi → Lungs
options.explanation: This sequence is incorrect, as the pharynx comes before the larynx.

options.text: Nose → Bronchi → Trachea → Larynx → Pharynx → Lungs
options.explanation: This sequence is incorrect, as the trachea comes before the bronchi and the larynx comes before the trachea.

questions.explanation: Air enters through the nose, then passes through the pharynx (throat), larynx (voice box), trachea (windpipe), bronchi (branches leading to lungs), and finally into the lungs.
questions.subject: upbo7-biology

questions.question: When we exhale, the diaphragm:

options.explanation: This action occurs during inhalation, not exhalation.
This is the correct action of the diaphragm during exhalation.
The diaphragm relaxes during exhalation, it does not contract.
The diaphragm moves upwards during exhalation, not downwards.

questions.explanation: During exhalation, the diaphragm relaxes and dome-shaped, moving upwards, which decreases the volume of the chest cavity and forces air out of the lungs.
questions.subject: upbo7-biology

questions.question: Consider the following statements about respiration: I. Aerobic respiration releases a significantly higher amount of energy than anaerobic respiration. II. Anaerobic respiration can occur in some organisms like yeast. III. The end products of aerobic respiration are ethanol and carbon dioxide. IV. Humans can perform both aerobic and anaerobic respiration. Which of the above statements are CORRECT?

options.explanation: Statement III is incorrect, so this option is not correct.
Statements I and II are also correct, so this option is not correct.
This is the correct combination of statements.
Statement III is incorrect, so this option is not correct.

questions.explanation: I. Correct. Aerobic respiration completely breaks down glucose, yielding much more ATP. II. Correct. Yeast performs alcoholic fermentation, which is a type of anaerobic respiration. III. Incorrect. Ethanol and carbon dioxide are end products of alcoholic fermentation (anaerobic respiration in yeast). Aerobic respiration produces carbon dioxide and water. IV. Correct. Humans primarily perform aerobic respiration, but muscle cells can temporarily switch to anaerobic respiration (producing lactic acid) during intense exercise.
questions.subject: upbo7-biology

questions.question: A biology experiment sets up two sealed jars. Jar A contains germinating seeds, and Jar B contains boiled (dead) seeds. After 24 hours, it is observed that the oxygen level in Jar A has decreased, and the carbon dioxide level has increased. What does this observation primarily indicate?

options.text: Photosynthesis is occurring in Jar A.
options.explanation: Photosynthesis would increase oxygen levels, not decrease them.

options.text: The seeds in Jar A are absorbing water.
options.explanation: Water absorption would not directly affect oxygen and carbon dioxide levels.

options.text: Respiration is occurring in the germinating seeds in Jar A.
options.explanation: This is the correct interpretation of the observation.

options.text: Transpiration is occurring in Jar A.
options.explanation: Transpiration is the process of water movement through plants, not directly related to oxygen and carbon dioxide levels.

questions.explanation: Germinating seeds are living and actively respiring. Respiration consumes oxygen and releases carbon dioxide. The decrease in oxygen and increase in carbon dioxide in Jar A directly demonstrates this process. Boiled seeds in Jar B would not show these changes as they are dead and not respiring.
questions.subject: upbo7-biology

questions.question: Why does a person's breathing rate increase significantly after vigorous physical activity, such as running?

options.text: To absorb more nitrogen from the atmosphere.
options.explanation: Nitrogen is not directly related to the increased breathing rate after exercise.

options.text: To increase the production of carbon dioxide for energy.
options.explanation: Carbon dioxide is a byproduct of respiration, not a goal of increased breathing rate.

options.text: To meet the increased oxygen demand of muscle cells and remove excess carbon dioxide.
options.explanation: This is the correct reason for the increased breathing rate after exercise.

options.text: To cool down the body temperature by evaporating more water.
options.explanation: While evaporation of water can help cool the body, it is not the primary reason for the increased breathing rate after exercise.

questions.explanation: During vigorous activity, muscle cells require more energy, which means they need more oxygen for aerobic respiration and produce more carbon dioxide as a waste product. Increased breathing rate and depth help to supply more oxygen to the blood and efficiently remove the accumulated carbon dioxide from the body.
questions.subject: upbo7-biology
